risks.title: Fluctuations in yen/dollar foreign exchange rates
risks.score_rationale: This risk is mentioned prominently in the Risk Factors section and detailed extensively in Item 7A. The company is significantly exposed through its Japan operations and substantial yen-denominated investments. Exchange rate fluctuations directly impact the translation of yen-denominated assets/liabilities into USD for reporting, and the company notes potential for significant cash strain at the parent company level from derivative settlements and collateral requirements. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Fluctuations in the yen/dollar exchange rate impact the value of Aflac Japan's yen-denominated assets and liabilities when translated to USD for financial reporting, and can create significant liquidity requirements for derivative settlements and collateral, particularly during yen strengthening periods.

risks.title: Interest rate risk on fixed income investments
risks.score_rationale: Interest rate risk is identified as a primary market risk factor affecting the company's investment portfolio. The company holds a significant portion of fixed maturity securities which are sensitive to rate changes. Item 7A explicitly identifies this as one of the primary market risks monitored regularly. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Changes in interest rates affect the fair value of the company's substantial portfolio of fixed maturity securities, potentially impacting investment returns and the company's financial position.

risks.title: Credit risk on fixed income securities
risks.score_rationale: The document indicates that a significant portion of the investment portfolio is composed of fixed maturity securities, exposing the company to counterparty credit risk. The company monitors credit risk through various strategies, suggesting material exposure. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: A substantial portion of Aflac's investment portfolio consists of fixed maturity securities and loans, creating exposure to credit risk from potential defaults by underlying issuers and borrowers.

risks.title: Geographic concentration of investments in Japan
risks.score_rationale: The company's Japan segment generates the vast majority of earnings and the investment portfolio shows significant concentration in yen-denominated securities. The MD&A indicates that Aflac Japan's functional currency is the yen and a material portion of the portfolio supports yen-denominated liabilities, creating concentration risk. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Aflac Japan represents the company's primary profit driver, and a material portion of the investment portfolio is concentrated in yen-denominated and Japan-based securities, creating vulnerability to Japan-specific economic conditions.

risks.title: Derivative and hedging program risks
risks.score_rationale: Item 7A details extensive use of foreign currency forwards, options, and other derivatives for hedging purposes. The company acknowledges rollover risk, basis risk, and the potential for significant derivative losses during periods of yen movement. The company notes explicit risks from shorter-duration derivatives hedging longer-duration investments. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Aflac uses foreign currency derivatives and hedging instruments to manage currency exposure, but these instruments introduce rollover risk, collateral requirements, and potential settlement losses, particularly during volatile currency movements.

risks.title: Liquidity strain from foreign exchange derivatives settlement
risks.score_rationale: Item 7A explicitly states that if yen strengthens significantly, this could cause cash strain at the parent company from derivative cash settlements and collateral requirements, and notes this could be significant depending on timing and severity of rate movements. The company manages this through ongoing hedging program adjustments. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Aflac's use of foreign currency derivatives to hedge yen exposure can create significant temporary liquidity demands at the parent company level during periods of yen strengthening, requiring cash for collateral and settlement obligations.

company_description: Aflac Incorporated, through its subsidiaries, provides supplemental health and life insurance products. It operates in two segments, Aflac Japan and Aflac U.S. The Aflac Japan segment offers cancer, medical, nursing care, whole life, and GIFT insurance products, as well as WAYS and child endowment, and Tsumitasu insurance products in Japan. Its Aflac U.S. segment provides accident, disability, cancer, critical illness, hospital indemnity, dental, vision, and life insurance products in the United States. The company also provides hearing, final expense, pet, Medicare supplement, supplemental dental and vision, short-term disability, and absence management insurance products, as well as cafeteria plans. It sells its products to individuals, families, and business owners through individual, independent corporate, and affiliated corporate agencies; banks; independent associates/career agents; and brokers. Aflac Incorporated was founded in 1955 and is headquartered in Columbus, Georgia.
